title: Hand Massage: A 3-Minute Routine for Typing and Phone Use — cv.cm
description: How to massage your hands and wrists after typing or phone use: palm, thumb base, fingers, forearm, a 3-minute routine, and signs of carpal tunnel to check.
h1: How do you massage your own hands?
answer: Use a little lotion and the thumb of your other hand. Press in small circles across the palm and the thick muscle at the base of the thumb, squeeze and slide along each finger, press the web between thumb and index finger, then knead the forearm on both sides. Use medium pressure for about 3 minutes per hand. Numbness or tingling at night needs a doctor, not massage.

sections.h: Why hands get tired, and what massage can do
body: Typing, using a mouse, holding a phone and gripping tools keep the same small muscles working for hours. The muscles that bend and straighten the fingers start in the forearm, so tired hands often come with a tight forearm too. Hours of scrolling also keep the thumb bent and busy.

Massage cannot fix a nerve or joint problem. Many people find that it eases tightness, warms stiff fingers and gives a useful pause from the keyboard. Pair it with breaks: change your grip, rest the hands in your lap, and stretch the fingers wide every half hour.

ul: Use a small amount of unscented hand cream or oil, about the size of a pea per hand, so the thumb glides without dragging the skin. Dry hands work for the pressure steps.
Rest the hand you are massaging on your thigh or a table, palm up, fully relaxed.
Pressure: light moves the skin only, medium moves the muscle, firm goes deeper but stays comfortable. On the hand, medium is right for most people.

body: Aim for 4 to 6 on a 1 to 10 scale: firm but not painful. A dull, pleasant ache is fine. Sharp pain, burning, or a tingling that shoots into the fingers means stop and use less pressure.

sections.h: Step by step: palm, thumb, fingers and forearm

ol: Palm: with the thumb of the other hand, make small, slow circles over the whole palm, from the heel of the hand up to the base of the fingers. Spend extra time on any tight spot.
Thumb base: the thick pad of muscle at the base of the thumb works hard when you text and grip. Press it in circles, then glide the thumb from the wrist toward the base of the thumb.
Pinky side: knead the muscle along the outer edge of the palm, below the little finger.

Fingers: hold the base of one finger between your thumb and index finger. Squeeze gently and slide to the tip, turning slightly as you go. Do each finger and the thumb twice. Do not crack or yank the joints.
Webbing: squeeze the soft web between each pair of fingers. Spend the most time on the web between the thumb and index finger, which is where `LI4` sits.
Back of the hand: glide the thumb in the grooves between the long hand bones, from the knuckles toward the wrist.
Wrist: make small circles around the wrist with your thumb, light pressure on the palm side, where the nerves and tendons are close to the skin.
Inner forearm: palm up. Knead the muscle from the wrist up to just below the elbow with your thumb or squeeze it with the whole hand. These are the muscles that bend the fingers.
Outer forearm: palm down. Knead the top of the forearm from the wrist to just below the elbow. These muscles straighten the fingers and work hard when you type.
Finish: stroke from the fingertips to the elbow three times, then shake the hand loosely.

sections.h: Two pressure points on the hand and wrist
body: Acupressure guides often add two points in this area. Locations follow the WHO Standard Acupuncture Point Locations (2008). A cun is a body-relative unit: 2 cun is about the width of your index, middle and ring fingers held together.

head: Point
Where it is
How to find it
How to press
rows: Back of the hand, beside the middle of the index-finger bone, on the thumb side
Press the thumb against the index finger. Near the top of the muscle bump, relax the hand and feel for the tender spot next to the bone
Opposite thumb on top, index finger under the palm. Squeeze toward the index-finger bone, 4 to 6 out of 10, 30 to 60 seconds
Inner forearm, 2 cun above the wrist crease, between the two central tendons
Lay three fingers across the wrist from the crease. Make a loose fist and bend the wrist slightly to see the two tendons
Thumb pad straight down, medium pressure only, 30 to 60 seconds. A nerve runs below: ease off if you feel tingling

body.note: If you are pregnant, ask your midwife or doctor before using acupressure. Traditional advice avoids firm pressure on `LI4` during pregnancy.

sections.h: A 3-minute routine for desk and phone users
body: Do this once or twice a day, or after a long typing session. To time it without watching the clock, you can use a timer, for example cv.cm's countdown set to 90 seconds per hand.

head: Step
What to do
Time per hand
rows: Small thumb circles over the palm and the thumb pad
Squeeze and slide along each finger and the thumb
Squeeze each web, hold the thumb web
Knead the inner then outer forearm, wrist to elbow
Long strokes to the elbow, then shake the hand loosely

body: Then stretch gently: hold one arm straight in front, palm up, and use the other hand to ease the fingers down and back until you feel a mild stretch in the inner forearm. Hold for 15 to 20 seconds. Repeat with the palm down to stretch the top of the forearm.

sections.h: Giving a hand massage to an older family member
body: A hand massage is a calm, simple way to spend time with an older parent or grandparent. Older skin is thinner and bruises more easily, and joints may be stiff or painful from arthritis.

ul: Ask first, and agree that they will tell you at once if anything is uncomfortable.
Sit facing them and rest their hand on a cushion or towel on their lap.
Use lotion and light to medium pressure. Glide; do not pinch or drag the skin.
Move around swollen, red or painful joints, not over them. Never pull or bend a finger further than it goes on its own.
Be very gentle if they take blood thinners, bruise easily, or have thin, fragile skin. Skip any area with a bruise, cut, rash or skin tear.
If they have diabetes or reduced feeling in the hands, check the skin before and after, and keep pressure light.
Five minutes per hand is plenty.

body: Studies of hand massage are small. In a 2013 trial with 42 adults with rheumatoid arthritis in the arms, people who received moderate-pressure massage from a therapist and did daily self-massage reported less pain and more grip strength after a month than people who received light-pressure massage. The study was small and not blinded, so treat it as a hint that medium pressure feels more useful than very light stroking.

NCCIH, the US government research centre for complementary health, says massage has been studied for several kinds of pain, mostly with weak or short-term evidence, and that the risk of harm appears low. Massage can be a pleasant self-care habit for tired hands. It does not treat carpal tunnel syndrome or arthritis.

sections.h: Safety: carpal tunnel, arthritis and when to see a doctor
body: Some hand symptoms are not muscle tiredness. The NHS lists these as signs of carpal tunnel syndrome, where a nerve is squeezed at the wrist: aching or pain in the fingers, hand or arm, numb hands, tingling or pins and needles, and a weak thumb or trouble gripping. Symptoms often come and go and tend to be worse at night.

ul: Numbness, tingling or weakness, especially at night: see a doctor. Do not press hard on the palm side of the wrist.

Stiff, swollen or painful finger joints, or a painful lump at the base of the thumb: this may be arthritis or tendon trouble. Massage the muscles around the joint gently, not the joint itself, and get it checked.
Do not massage over broken skin, a rash, a burn, a fresh bruise, a recent injury or a hot, red, swollen area.

body.note: Get urgent medical help if you have severe wrist pain, heard a snap or crack at the time of an injury, cannot move the wrist or hold things, the wrist has changed shape or colour, a lump is very painful, hot or red, you have lost feeling in part or all of the hand, or you feel unwell with a fever. These can be signs of a fracture or an infection.

body: See a doctor or physiotherapist if hand or wrist pain lasts more than a few weeks or keeps you from working, even if massage seems to help for a while.

faq.q: Is hand massage good for arthritis?
faq.a: Small studies suggest gentle to moderate massage around the joints may ease pain and stiffness for a while. Do not press on swollen, red or hot joints, and follow the advice of your doctor or physiotherapist.

faq.q: Can hand massage help carpal tunnel syndrome?
faq.a: There is no good evidence that massage treats carpal tunnel syndrome. The NHS suggests wrist splints at night, fewer activities that bend the wrist, and seeing a GP if symptoms get worse or do not go away.

faq.q: How often should I massage my hands?
faq.a: Once or twice a day for a few minutes is enough. Short breaks every 30 to 60 minutes of typing also help.

faq.q: What is the pressure point between the thumb and index finger?
faq.a: It is Hegu (`LI4`), on the back of the hand beside the middle of the index-finger bone. Many people press it for tension, but avoid firm pressure there if you are pregnant.

faq.q: Why do my hands hurt after using my phone?
faq.a: Holding a phone keeps the thumb and wrist bent and the small hand muscles working for a long time. Switch hands, rest the phone on a surface, and take breaks. See a doctor if you have numbness, tingling or weakness.
